summary:
SPIRIT is a PC exploration game that lets players experience space through the robotic explorers that made discovery possible. Players become a curious spirit born from fragments of these machines’ experiences, beginning their journey by connecting with NASA’s Opportunity rover on Mars.

Using the rover’s real capabilities and limitations, players investigate rocks, examine their surroundings, and search for clues of ancient water. A connected skill tree introduces scientific abilities and reveals relationships between robotic explorers, creating pathways for future adventures.

SPIRIT addresses the challenge by turning scientific discoveries and mission stories into interactive experiences. Designed primarily for ages 10–15, it brings meaningful science into play without overwhelming players.

The project matters because it makes space exploration personal and accessible, encouraging young people to ask questions, investigate evidence, and see scientific discovery as something they can participate in.
details:
SPIRIT is a PC exploration game developed by AstroNot, a team of six people with backgrounds in programming, graphic design, storytelling, and business. Designed primarily for ages 10–15, it combines a fictional story with real space exploration to make scientific discovery engaging and accessible.

Players follow Spirit, a curious being born from fragments of experiences left behind by robotic explorers. Although Spirit carries memories of extraordinary missions, it has never explored for itself. Its journey begins by connecting with NASA’s Opportunity rover on Mars, allowing players to experience exploration through the rover’s perspective, capabilities, and limitations.

The gameplay is designed around observing, investigating, and interpreting the environment. Players examine rocks, investigate unusual formations, and look for evidence of ancient water. Scientific instruments become tools for answering questions, giving players a reason to understand what each instrument does. The experience connects actions with discoveries instead of relying entirely on explanations or quizzes.

A central part of the design is a connected skill tree. Scientific abilities reveal relationships between robotic explorers through shared instruments, engineering principles, or investigative methods. The initial experience focuses on Opportunity, while the wider concept allows these connections to introduce additional missions and destinations in future versions.

Our development stack combines JavaScript and React for the interface, Three.js through React Three Fiber and Drei for the 3D environment, and Zustand for shared game state and progression. Vite supports development and builds, while Git and GitHub support collaboration and version control.

SPIRIT’s creative approach combines an emotional narrative with exploration grounded in science. The fictional spirit gives players a personal connection to machines that might otherwise feel distant, while the rover’s real constraints help shape meaningful gameplay. The skill tree also presents space missions as connected parts of a larger history of discovery.

Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, age-appropriate explanations, intuitive controls, visual clarity, performance, and the time available to build a focused prototype. We also considered how to balance educational depth with freedom and enjoyment.

Our intended impact is to encourage curiosity, observation, and reasoning from evidence. By letting players participate in the process of discovery, SPIRIT aims to make space science memorable and inspire them to explore the real missions behind the experience.
